Main.sentence: A prisoner exchange or prisoner swap is a deal between opposing sides in a conflict to release prisoners: ___E:prisoners of war U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prisoner_of_war)___ , ___E:spies U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spy)___ , ___E:hostages U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hostage)___ , etc. Sometimes, ___E:dead bodies U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cadaver)___ are involved in an exchange.

Prisoners exchanged occurred throughout history; a number of large exchanges took places, for example, during the 8th century or so in the Middle East region (see ___E:Arab–Byzantine prisoner exchanges U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arab%E2%80%93Byzantine_prisoner_exchanges)___ ).

Under the ___E:Geneva Conventions U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Geneva_Conventions)___ , prisoners who cannot contribute to the ___E:war effort U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/War_effort)___ because of ___E:illness or disability U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wounded_in_action)___ are entitled to be repatriated to their home country.
That is regardless of number of prisoners so affected; the detaining power cannot refuse a genuine request.
Under the ___E:Geneva Convention (1929) U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Geneva_Convention_on_Prisoners_of_War_(1929))___ , this is covered by Articles 68 to 74, and the annex.

One of the largest exchange programmes was run for ___E:prisoners of war U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prisoners_of_war_in_World_War_II)___ by the ___E:International Red Cross U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_Committee_of_the_Red_Cross)___ during ___E:World War II U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_War_II)___ under these terms.  [failed verification] Under the ___E:Third Geneva Convention U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Third_Geneva_Convention)___ of 1949, that is covered by Articles 109 to 117.

The ___E:Second World War in Yugoslavia U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_War_II_in_Yugoslavia)___ saw a brutal struggle between the armed forces of the ___E:Third Reich U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Third_Reich)___ and the ___E:communist-led Partisans U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yugoslav_Partisans)___ .

Despite that, the two sides negotiated prisoner exchanges virtually from the beginning of the war. Under extraordinary circumstances, these early contacts evolved into a formal exchange agreement, centered on the creation of a neutral zone, possibly the only such in occupied Europe, where prisoners were regularly swapped until late April 1945, saving several thousand lives.
